reason: Reproduced exactly: on the across measure the [data-lead="true"] tick's centre sits 28.00px left of its own item anchor at 1920, 1440, 1280, 1024 and 768&layout=across, on paper and on ink, while all six other ticks measure dx=0.00 — computed left is -28px from the (0,5,0) [data-medium="sheet"|"full"] rule at src/timeline.css:1829 beating the (0,4,0) across rule at src/across.css:169, and the item's own leader stem (::after) starts at left:0, so the one filled indigo mark visibly detaches from the stem that claims it (confirmed in a crop). The scale arithmetic holds — 1610px/79d at 1920 makes it read 1.37 days early, 476px/79d at 768-across makes it 4.65 days early. This is the SAME defect as lead-tick-off-its-own-date (same element, same 28px, same specificity cause, same one-line fix); two seats sighted it independently on the two axes of the same argument.
sharpenedFix: Drop the `top: var(--rule-y)` half — measured, every across tick including the lead one already sits at dy = --rule-y = 122px, because src/across.css:170 wins `top` on order against src/timeline.css:711 and the [data-medium] rule at :1829 sets only `left`. So the whole fix is one declaration: `[data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-item[data-lead="true"] .b-tick { left: 0; }` (0,6,0), which I applied in-page and re-measured: dx goes to 0.00 for the lead and nothing else on either axis moves. Also note the stem clearance is 28px, not the 24px stated.
